page-title.purpose: The single <h1> on every page. Uppercase Archivo 600 in maroon. One treatment across all six pages.

section-title.purpose: Every <h2>, always emitted by SheetHead. Maroon on light plates, sun on dark plates.

sub-title.purpose: Product names, project titles, pull-quotes, footer company name.

figure.purpose: Headline quantities in Azeret Mono with tabular numerals: stats, client count, selected capacity, contact phone numbers.

lede.purpose: The one paragraph under a section head, capped at 64ch.

label.purpose: The only small-type voice: uppercase Azeret Mono at 0.15em tracking. Kickers, table headers, field labels, button text, hints, citations.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the build.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and border-colour state changes on links, buttons, chips, fields.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: Declared for longer transitions; currently unused by any component.

motion.name: camera-lerp
motion.purpose: Frame-rate-independent camera easing toward a route's station. Forced to 1 under prefers-reduced-motion so the camera snaps.

motion.name: pour-lerp
motion.purpose: Clipping-plane fill and mould-panel strike in the casting sequence.

motion.name: resize-lerp
motion.purpose: Tank scale change when a capacity is selected in the configurator.

motion.name: reduced-motion-clamp
motion.purpose: Global CSS clamp under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

narrative.overview:
The site is a working precast concrete yard in Coimbatore at five in the afternoon, and the visitor is standing in it. One persistent WebGL canvas is fixed behind every page: rows of cast sumps stacked two high on compacted earth, a gantry crane crossing the haze, a maroon lorry loaded at the gate, dust drifting in the light, and a low sun off frame left throwing shadows toward the camera. Navigation never swaps a backdrop — it moves the camera to a different station in the same yard. The DOM is not part of that world: it writes on top of it, on opaque slabs of daylight-coloured card.

The tone is a contractor's drawing set, not a brochure. Everything is square — there is not one non-zero border-radius in the build. Separation is done with hairlines and a maroon top rule, never with shadow, never with transparency. Every number in the interface is set in Azeret Mono with tabular numerals, so figures read as measured quantities rather than marketing. Brand maroon is the plate rule and the call stamp; the sun belongs to the render and is allowed into the DOM only on dark plates.

The build refuses the default WebGL product page — a spinning grey model on a studio sweep. Even the two small inline scenes mount a sky dome and exponential fog so a pour happens outdoors under the same sun. It also refuses decoration that carries no fact: no gradients, no glass, no photograph standing in for a product that has none.
keyCharacteristics: One persistent 3D yard behind an opaque, scrolling DOM — never blur, never alpha
Zero corner radius; hairline rules and a 3px maroon top rule instead of elevation
Archivo for prose, Azeret Mono for every figure and every label
Uppercase 0.15em-tracked mono labels as the only small-type voice
The phone number is the primary action and is present at every scroll position
Full function with zero 3D: WebGL, quality and reduced-motion are all gated

rules.name: The Opaque Plate Rule
rules.body: --plate and --plate-dark are fully opaque hex — no alpha channel, no backdrop-filter, no opacity on a plate, ever. Text over a live 3D scene must never be modulated by what the camera happens to be looking at, and blurring a running canvas is the single most expensive thing this site could do. Separation from the yard comes from the maroon top rule.

rules.name: The Orange Text Rule
rules.body: --orange is for chrome that is not read (focus rings, underlines, slider thumbs). Any orange that is read on a light ground uses --orange-text. Setting --orange as a text colour on --paper is a contrast failure.

rules.name: The Sun-On-Dark Rule
rules.body: --sun may only be used on --plate-dark. On paper it fails contrast; on ink it is the point of the world.

rules.name: The One Palette Rule
rules.body: No hex literal may appear in a component. If the render needs a colour it comes from PALETTE; if the DOM needs one it comes from a :root token; and when the same material exists in both, the two values are identical by hand.

rules.name: The Single H1 Rule
rules.body: Every page has exactly one <h1>, and it is .page-title. Four different H1 treatments across six pages was the loudest inconsistency in the first pass; a seventh page adds a seventh .page-title, not a seventh idea.

rules.name: The Mono Figure Rule
rules.body: If it is a quantity — litres, years, a count, a phone number, a step index, a spec-sheet size — it is set in --font-fig with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Prose never carries a figure in the text face.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Uppercase in Archivo is reserved for titles. Every other uppercase string in the build is Azeret Mono at 0.6875rem with 0.15em tracking. There is no third small-type style.

rules.name: The Gap Rule
rules.body: Plates must leave gaps. A page whose plates run edge to edge with no .section breathing space has hidden the product; the yard between the plates is what the site is selling.

rules.name: The Narrow Plate Rule
rules.body: A plate that carries reading matter stays narrow — .lede is capped at 64ch, .hero-plate at 40rem, notes at 34–56ch. Wide plates are reserved for schedules and grids.

rules.name: The Flat-DOM Rule
rules.body: Elevation is a property of the yard, not of the page. If a DOM element needs to feel lifted, it becomes a plate — it never grows a shadow.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Hairline Rule
rules.body: Exactly two rule weights exist. --rule (1px, #cabfa9) separates rows inside a block; --rule-strong (1px, #8a7f6b) separates blocks and frames canvases and images. A third weight is a new decision, not a tweak.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: Radius is zero. A rounded corner in this world is a different product being sold.

rules.name: The One-Sided Border Rule
rules.body: A border may be one-sided, but only as a hairline or as the plate's 3px top rule. A thick coloured bar down one side of a block is decoration the system never asked for — a 3px maroon left border was removed from .about-testimonial for exactly this.

rules.name: The Same Yard Rule
rules.body: Navigation moves the camera; it never swaps a scene. Any new page gets a station in the existing yard.

rules.name: The Same Sun Rule
rules.body: Every canvas in the build mounts GroundAndSky (or the main SkyDome) and lights with PALETTE.sunLight from a low angle. A studio sweep behind a floating grey model is the exact artifact this world exists to refuse.

dos: Do put every new surface on a .plate inside .sheet inside .section, and let the section padding leave 4–8rem of open yard between plates.
Do add a camera station to STATIONS for any new route, and pick pos/look so the plate does not cover the busiest part of the frame.
Do set every quantity in --font-fig with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
Do use .page-title for the page's single <h1> and SheetHead for every section head.
Do gate any new canvas on hasWebGL(), wrap it in LazyCanvas, run it frameloop="demand", and call invalidate() on every state change and every settling frame.
Do honour prefersReducedMotion() by arriving at the end state immediately rather than by animating faster.
Do keep every interactive target at 44px minimum, 48px for buttons and fields.
Do take colours from :root in the DOM and from PALETTE in the render, and keep the two identical for any material that exists in both.
Do render a labelled empty slot when a fact or an asset does not exist.
donts: Don't use backdrop-filter, blur(), or any alpha on a plate over the canvas. Text legibility would then depend on the current camera frame, and blurring a live canvas is the most expensive effect this site could ship.
Don't add a box-shadow anywhere in the DOM. Shadows belong to the sun in the render; the interface is flat by construction.

Don't put a thick one-sided coloured border on a block. A 3px maroon left border was removed from .about-testimonial for exactly this — it was decoration that carried no information, and the hairline border-top every other block uses replaced it.
Don't use a gradient as decoration. The only ramp in the build is the sky dome's vertex colour, which is the physical sky.
Don't hard-code a colour, a font stack or a spacing value in a component. If the value does not exist as a token, decide whether it should.
Don't state a dimension, a capacity, a client count or a year that is not in lib/site.js.
Don't substitute a photograph for a product that has none, and don't crop another product's photo to fill the gap.
Don't put --orange on light-ground text (use --orange-text) or --sun on a light plate (dark plates only).
Don't mount a second inline canvas on a page that already has one, and don't let the persistent yard become a third live context on the same route.
Don't let a canvas take pointer events outside a marked interactive stage, or become a scroll or width source.
